incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency spike for hosted-api/us-west-2 detected (>=1.2s for 3m). Metric: infrastructure.latency.p99. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/latency/hosted?orgId=1&from=now-15m

maria (oncall): I’m taking this. seeing customer-facing latency? which routes? :eyes:

ajay (eng-sre): Quick look: p95 ~ 420ms, p99 hit 1.45s. Spike started ~2112233280. Mainly text-generation routes (/v1/generate) and streaming sessions show stalls.

kevin (eng-runtime): I’m pulling traces from the stream router. initial smoke: KV cache churn high + some gRPC retries. Might be an OOM GC on the model worker or kernel stall.

maria (oncall): @kevin can you paste the top traces and any worker logs? I’ll check routing and autoscale.

kevin (eng-runtime): trace ids: trace-0x9a2f, trace-0x9b3c. Top span shows `serve_step->kernel_execute` long tail ~1.2s. Worker stderr snippet:
```
[2026-03-14T20:21:45Z] WARN kv_cache: eviction_pressure=0.82
[2026-03-14T20:21:45Z] ERROR runtime::exec: kernel stall detected, duration=1180ms, model=redwood-13b-quant
```

ajay (eng-sre): Running quick DB query for request distribution: `SELECT count(*) FROM requests WHERE region='us-west-2' AND ts > now() - interval '10 minutes' GROUP BY route ORDER BY count DESC;`
Result: `/v1/generate` 32k, `/v1/chat` 8k, `/v1/embeddings` 600. p99 concentrated on `/v1/generate`.

sophia (product): Any customer impact yet? we need to surface to CS if > 5% of production requests degraded.

maria (oncall): Support (cc @sophia) says increased client-side timeouts reported by 2 enterprise customers. Not widespread yet but definitely a user-visible degradation.

ajay (eng-sre): Quick check of canary deploys: we had a runtime patch (kernel scheduling tweak) rolled to canary group at 20:05 UTC (~2112233305). Canary traffic 5%. Canary metrics show p99 elevated for canary instances as well.

kevin (eng-runtime): That points at the kernel tweak. Options: 1) Roll back canary, 2) Force fallback to alternate execution path (less optimized), 3) Scale up dedicated pool to absorb backlog. I'll prepare rollback if we want it.

maria (oncall): Rolling back a canary is higher risk but faster. @ajay can you estimate how many requests are currently above SLO (p99 threshold 1.0s)?

ajay (eng-sre): Query: `SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE latency>1000) AS breached, count(*) AS total FROM recent_requests WHERE region='us-west-2' AND ts > now() - interval '5 minutes';`
Result: breached=1750, total=24800 -> ~7.1% above 1s SLO.

sophia (product): 7% is enough to notify prioritized customers. Drafting a heads-up now.

maria (oncall): We need immediate mitigation. Plan: 1) rollback canary to previous runtime version, 2) enable fallback execution path on all workers, 3) scale pool +2 nodes. I'll coordinate steps. Pager status: escalate if rollback fails.

maria (oncall): /infra run rollback-runtime --canary-id=canary-20260314-20:05

deploy-bot: accepted: rollback job queued (job-id: rb-2112233346). Estimated completion ~60s.

log-bot: streaming recent error/latency logs to thread. sample:
```
[2026-03-14T20:22:10Z] request_id=abcd1234 route=/v1/generate p99=1450ms worker=worker-07
[2026-03-14T20:22:12Z] request_id=abcd1237 stream_stall=true stall_duration=900ms
```

kevin (eng-runtime): I’m also toggling fallback execution mode: `runtimectl set global execution_mode=fallback-safe` -> applying. This switches to slower but stable kernel path.

ajay (eng-sre): Scaling action: `/infra scale pool inference-dedicated-usw2 +2`

infra-bot: scale request accepted, provisioning 2 nodes (node-type: a100-40gb). ETA 2m.

maria (oncall): Pagerduty: marking incident as P1 and escalating to SRE lead if rollback doesn't clear in 5m. @pagerduty update status: paged.

pagerduty: escalation sent to oncall-sre-lead. status=triggered.

(deploy-bot): rollback rb-2112233346 completed: canary reverted to runtime v1.8.3. Canary traffic now on previous version.

ajay (eng-sre): Early signal: canary p99 dropping to ~0.9s for canary instances. Global p99 trending down: 1.45 -> 1.05 in the last 90s.

kevin (eng-runtime): Fallback path active on 60% of workers; autoscale nodes provisioning. I’m watching KV cache eviction rates; they should normalize as kernel returns to stable behavior.

maria (oncall): Customer impact: ajay reports ~1750 requests breached in last 5m; support flagged 2 enterprise customers with timeouts. Sophia drafting customer note.

sophia (product): Draft ready, will send post-ops update once we have sustained p99 <1.0s for 30m.

log-bot: infra-bot: nodes provisioned: node-391, node-392 added to pool.

ajay (eng-sre): Current global numbers: p95 380ms, p99 980ms, error rate normal. Tail latencies reduced but monitoring for stalls.

maria (oncall): Great. Marking immediate mitigation successful. We'll keep this thread open for postmortem. Action items: - kevin follow up on kernel regression root cause - ajay provide detailed query logs for SLO breach counts - ops to run 30m watch.

kevin (eng-runtime): I’ll open an issue linking the kernel change diff and attach traces. Initial hypothesis: a scheduling heuristic introduced a path that increases stalls under high KV churn.

ajay (eng-sre): Saved queries + raw request ids for sample traces: `[['abcd1234','abcd1237','abce0009']]` (will attach to the postmortem doc).

maria (oncall): Thank you all. Re-opening only if we see fresh spikes. Leaving monitoring for 30m. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated -> monitoring. p99 back to <1.0s. Time to mitigate: ~3 minutes after rollback + fallback + scaling.

sophia (product): Noting follow-up: customer comms, postmortem, and a signal to delay the kernel change from canary->prod until root cause fixed.

maria (oncall): Creating incident ticket for postmortem: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OPS-6421. Assigning kevin + ajay.

kevin (eng-runtime): Acknowledged. I’ll attach runtime traces and config diff.

ajay (eng-sre): Will prepare SLO breach graph and query dump.

maria (oncall): Thanks team. Closing handoff. If anyone sees recurrence ping this thread.

sophia (product): one more: please add a customer-visible root cause note draft to the ticket.

maria (oncall): Roger. End of thread for now.
